State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
Taffe Tractors & Equipments Ltd. vs Murari Narsing Bhosale on 31 January, 2011
1 F.A.No.2455-05

 STATE CONSUMER DISPUTE REDRESSAL COMMISSION,
 MUMBAI, CIRCUIT BENCH AT AURANGABAD.

 Date of filing : 13.12.2005
 Date of Order: 31.01.2011

FIRST APPEAL NO.2455 OF 2005
IN COMPLAINT CASE NO. 153 OF 2004
DISTRICT CONSUMER FORUM: LATUR.

Taffe Tractors & Equipments Ltd.
Chennai,
On behalf of Chief Director,
35, New Gyanbakam High Road, Chennai. ... Appellant

 //VERSUS//

1. Murari Narsing Bhosale
 R/o. Halaki, Tal. Shirur
 Anantpal, Dist. Latur.

2. Jai Sai Tractors,
 Nanded Naka, Udgir.

3. Monohar Bhimrao Patwai
 Jai Sai Tractors,
 Nanded Naka, Udgir.

4. National Insurance Co. Ltd.
 on behalf of Br. Manager,
 Hanuman Chowk, Latur.

5. I.C.I.C.I. Bank Ltd.
 1st Floor, Pad Equipment
 Tapdiya Circle, Nirala Bazar,
 Samartha Nagar, Aurangabad. ... Respondents

 Coram : Shri.S.G.Deshmukh, Hon`ble Presiding Judicial Member.
Mrs. Uma S.Bora, Hon`ble Member.
Shri. K. B. Gawali, Hon'ble Member.
Present: Adv. Smt. Vaishali Jadhav, for appellant.
Adv. Shri. Gaikwad for respondent no.1.
Adv. Shri. Ambhore for respondent no.4.
2 F.A.No.2455-05
:: ORAL ORDER ::
Per Shri. K. B. Gawali, Hon'ble Member
1. TAFE Tractors and Farms Equipment Limited, Chennai
through its Chief Director who was original respondent no.1 has
preferred the present appeal against the Judgment and Order dated
30.09.2005 passed by District Consumer Forum, Latur in complaint case
No. 153/2004.
2. The background of this appeal in brief is as under:-
Respondent No.1 Shri. Morari S/o. Narsing Bhosale i.e.
original complainant before the Forum is an agriculturist of village Halki
Tq. Shirur Anantpal Dist. Latur. He is also physical handicapped person.
The appellant is the manufacturer of Tafe tractor in question where as
the respondent no. 2 & 3 are the dealers of the said manufacturing
company. Respondent No.4 is the National Insurance Company and
Respondent No.5 is the I.C.I.C.I. Bank Limited, who is alleged to be
financer in respect of tractor in question. The appellant and respondent
no. 2 & 3 have jointly published an advertisement in 'Daily Lokmat'
dated 29.09.2003 regarding good performance of the said tractor, and
they sent their representative named Vishwanath Jadhav to the village
Halki who visited the complainant and gave assurance regarding good
quality, performance and about free services of the tractor. On behalf of
respondent no. 2 & 3 it was also represented that on depositing of the 10
% amount of the total price of the tractor the tractor will be given in
possession and the remaining amount will be taken as loan from
Respondent No.5. It was also contended that if the tractor is purchased
before 31.12.2003 the TVS Suzuki motor cycle will be given free of cost
along with the said Gajraj Tractor. The respondent no.1/complainant
accordingly on 03.11.2003 paid Rs.17,105/- towards booking of the
tractor with respondent no. 2 & 3. Afterwards on 19.12.2003 he also
deposited further amount of Rs. 40,205/- with the respondent no. 2 & 3.
The tractor, Gajraj-60 HP Tafe-5900 D-I model as manufactured by
respondent no.1 was delivered on 11.01.2004 by the respondent no. 2 &
3 to the respondent no.1 and on the same day his signatures were
3 F.A.No.2455-05
obtained on the loan proposal but, the name of the Bank was not
disclosed to him. Respondent no. 2 & 3 also represented that the
insurance premium amount was paid by them to the respondent no.4. It
is alleged by respondent no.1 that he was not given the details regarding
the price of tractor and the loan amount sanctioned and disbursed. It is
alleged by respondent no.1 that on 24.02.2004 the respondent no.1 paid
amount of Rs.1,10,000/- to the respondent no. 2 & 3 as they had
directed the said payment on 11.01.2004. No receipt was however given
for the said amount.
3. It is alleged by respondent no.1 that within a weeks time from the
date of delivery i.e. 11.01.2004 the tractor was found to be not
functioning properly and it had various manufacturing defects, such as
leakage of oil at the head of the tractor, the clutch plates were not
working, Diesel meter, temperature meter and adometer were also not
working. Therefore on 19.01.2004 he approached with tractor to the
respondent no.2 & 3 and after two days he got the said tractor repaired.
However, the defects were not removed and again on 25.01.2004 the
tractor stopped working because the clutch plates were damaged,
therefore he took the tractor to respondent no. 2 & 3 and the same was
repaired. Again on 04.02.2004 there were complaints regarding the non-
functioning of the tractor and he took the same to respondent no. 2 & 3
who advised him to get the same repaired from other garage at Latur
since their mechanic is not on duty on that day. Again on 07.02.2004 the
clutch plate of the tractor were got repaired from the respondent no. 2 &
3 and bill of amounting to Rs. 2,990/- were paid, thus about 14 times
the tractor was to be repaired with the respondent no. 2 & 3 and also at
private garage as per advise of respondent no. 2 & 3 and total
expenditure incurred for repairs was to the tune of Rs. 33,599/-.
4. It is also the case of the respondent no.1 that there was a
variance in the engine number. The said number recorded on bill of the
tractor, & R.T.O. record was said to be S-433062394 whereas the same
was embossed on bonnet of the tractor was 062202. He further alleged
that the said tractor was not new one, but was of resale. He submitted
4 F.A.No.2455-05
that earlier day the same tractor was sold to one Shr8i. Arvind Jaypal
Reddy R/o. Tondchir Tq. Udgir Dist. Latur in the month of March-2003.
However due to oil leakage and other manufacturing defects, he returned
back the said tractor to respondent no.2 & 3 in August-2003. Hence, it is
alleged that the appellant and respondent no. 2 & 3 have cheated and
defraud him and have played unfair trade practice. Due to dis-
functioning of the tractor he could not use it for 27 days from the date of
delivery, till the date of filing the complaint with the District Forum. With
all these allegations he filed complaint with the Forum on 17.06.2004 to
direct the appellant and respondent no. 2 & 3 to deliver the tractor of the
same model in place of old tractor as it is having manufacturing defects.
In addition he also prayed to direct the appellant and respondent no. 2, 3
& 4 to pay individually and jointly Rs. 4,00,000/- towards compensation
along with the interest @ 18 % p.a. from the date of complaint till
realization. He also prayed directing appellant and respondent no. 2 to 4
to pay the cost of the complaint to the tune of Rs. 10,000/-.
5. The respondent no.1/complainant has also filed before the
Forum affidavit of Shri. Shivaji Gangadhar the mechanic of Shivkripa
Garage, Nanded Road, Latur regarding the defects in the said tractor
along with the affidavit of proprietor of the said garage named Shri.
Gopal Janardhan Kadam. In addition he has also filed affidavit of Shri.
V. K. Kulkarni who is automobile engineer working as a Surveyor & Loss
Assessor regarding the manufacturing defects of the tractor in question.
6. Respondent no. 2, 3 & 4 appeared before the Forum and
resisted the claim of respondent no. 1. Respondent no. 2 & 3 have
admitted that they have delivered the said tractor to the respondent no. 1
however; they denied that it had manufacturing defects. They have also
denied that the old tractor in place of new tractor was given to the
respondent no.1 as alleged. They also denied that amount of
Rs. 1,00,000/- was given to them. It was contended by the respondent
no. 2 & 3 that he was given the tractor in a good condition and he was
doing the business with the said tractor. But, malafied intention he filed
5 F.A.No.2455-05
the complaint before Forum and they should be awarded the cost of Rs.
5,000/-.
7. Respondent no. 4 i.e. National Insurance Company denied
that they have received any insurance premium and there was no
contract with the respondent no.1 and therefore they are not liable for
any damages, as claimed by the respondent no.1 in his complaint.
8. Forum below on the basis of the available record and after
hearing the parties hold the respondent no.1 solely responsible for the
manufacturing defect in the tractor and have passed the Judgment &
Order in question. The Forum has allowed the complaint partly and
directed respondent no.1 i.e. appellant to replace new tractor to the
respondent no.1 in place of earlier Gajraj Tractor OR to pay
Rs. 4,49,515/- with the interest @ 9 % p.a. from the date of filing of the
complaint to the respondent no.1. It has also directed to the respondent
no. 2 & 3 individually and jointly to pay Rs. 2,000/- towards the cost of
the complaint.
9. Aggrieved by the said Judgment and Order passed by the
Forum below the appellant company has field the present appeal.
Notices were issued to the appellant as well as all the
respondents. Adv. Smt. Vaishali Jadhav, appeared for appellant, Adv.
Shri. P.M. Gaikwad appeared for Respondent no.1, Adv. Shri. S. V.
Varad, for Respondent no. 2 & 3, Adv. Shri. M. M. Ambhore, appeared for
respondent no.4 and Adv. Shri. U. N. Shete, for respondent no.5.
10. The case was finally heard on 24.01.2011. We heard learned
counsel Smt. Vaishali Jadhav for the appellant, learned counsel
Shri. Gaikwad for respondent no.1 and learned counsel Shri. Ambhore
for respondent no.4. The learned counsel for the appellant contended
that the Forum below has passed the Judgment & Order exparte against
them. No notice was served to the company and without giving an
opportunity to here the order under appeal was passed by Forum below.
She referred to the reply as given against the first issue by the Forum
that whether the non-applicant have sold old tractor in place of new one
and by that committed unfair trade practice. Against this issue the
6 F.A.No.2455-05
Forum in its reply has hold responsible only respondent no. 2 & 3. Even
in the reply against the issue no.3 regarding variance and engine number
the Forum has held that responsible the respondent no.1 along with 2
and 3. However, in the final order only the appellant has been held
responsible and directed to replace the tractor or to pay the price of the
tractor with interest and no order is passed against respondent no. 2 & 3
who are the dealers of the said tractor. She also submitted that, Shri
Vijay Kulkarni is an automobile engineer and therefore his affidavit of the
manufacturing defects in the tractor can not be relied upon. In her
written argument she has also raised one objection that as per Sec. 13
(b) of C. P. Act, 1986 the vehicle was not sent to any workshop for
obtaining independent expert opinion regarding the alleged defects in the
tractor by the Forum below.
In support of her submission she has relied
upon the judgment of National Commission in respect of
Tata Engg. &
Locomotive Co. Ltd. Vs. Sunil Bhasin
- 2008 (2) CPR 271 (NC) in which it
is held that as per the procedure provided under Sec. 13 (b) of the Act
such vehicle should be sent to any workshop for independent opinion.
She has also referred to the unreported judgment of the Commission in
F.A. No. 1907/05 decided on 22.01.2010 in which it is held that for
proving the manufacturing defects of a car as was subject matter in that
complaint was ought to have been referred to the experts opinion as per
the procedure provided under 13 (b) of C. P. Act. On the basis of this
pleadings she contended that the Forums' order in question being not as
per law the same may be quashed and the case be remanded to the
Forum to decide the case afresh by giving sufficient opportunity to the
appellant.
11. On the other hand, the learned counsel for respondent no.1
argued that within 7 days of the delivery of the tractor in question it
started dis-functioning and time and again the respondent no.1 had to
take the tractor for repairs to the respondent no. 2 & 3 and even to
private garage. It was also argued that the respondent no.1 was given the
old tractor in place of new tractor. There was also variance in the engine
number and thus the respondent no.1 was defraud and cheated by the
7 F.A.No.2455-05
appellant and his dealer i. e. Respondent no.2 & 3. He has relied upon
two judgments of State Commissions in support of his submissions i)
Kerala State Commission, Thiruvananthapuram, in respect of M/s. Digital
Information System Vs. M. G. Rajesh and others in A- 913 & 915/1999
decided on 19.09.2000 and reported in II (2001) CPJ 284, in which it is
held that defective goods either to be replaced or the purchase amount
should be refunded with interest and necessary compensation, ii)
Maharashtra State Commission, Bombay in
Gopanlal Sohanlal Chandak
Vs. State of Maharashtra and Others
, reported in I (1994) CPJ 42. In this
case defective jeep was sold and therefore compensation and refund of
the amount with interest was awarded. On the basis of his pleadings the
learned counsel for respondent no.1 fully supported the judgment passed
by the Forum below.
12. The learned counsel for the respondent no.4 i.e. National
Insurance Company argued that no premium in respect of this tractor
was received by the company and hence they are not liable to pay any
claim.
13. On the basis of the available record and the pleadings as
putforth by the learned counsel of appellant and respondent no. 1 & 4. It
is observed that there is no dispute that the respondent
no.1/complainant has purchased the tractor of Gajraj-60 HP TAFFE-
5900 D-I model bearing registration No. MH-24/D-1827 from the
respondent no. 2 & 3 from the dealers and the appellant is the
manufacturer of the said tractor. The delivery of the said tractor was
given to the appellant on 11.01.2004 by the respondent no. 2 & 3. It is
revealed that various defects were found in the said tractor just after 7
days of its delivery. Respondent no. 1 had to take the said tractor
frequently to the respondent no. 2 & 3 for its repair. The said tractor was
also repaired from the private garages. The respondent no.1 has brought
on record that from the date of delivery i.e. 11.01.2004 till the filing of
complaint dated 17.06.2004 i.e. period about 5 months the tractor was
to be repaired 14 times and the total repair charges spent by him were
8 F.A.No.2455-05
Rs. 33,599/-. Due to this frequent repair the tractor was not in use for
about a month.
14. It is also the case of the respondent no.1 that the respondent no.2
& 3 i.e. dealers of the tractor had given him the old tractor instead of new
one. It is submitted that the said tractor was earlier sold to Shri. Jaypal
Govind Reddy in the March-2003 by the respondent no. 2 & 3, however
due to defects of oil leakage and other problems he returned the said
tractor to the respondent no. 2 & 3 in the month of March-2003 and the
same tractor was resold to the complainant i.e. respondent no.1. It is
also revealed that there is a variance of the engine number i.e. recorded
with RTO and on the tractor bill which is S-433062394 whereas the
engine number as embossed on bonnet of the tractor is 062202. The
respondent no.1 has submitted the affidavit of one Shri Gopal Janardhan
who is proprietor of Shivkripa Garage at Latur and also Shri Shivaji
Gangadhar Changwal who is the mechanic of Shivkripa Garage, Latur.
Both of them in their affidavit have submitted that the tractor of
respondent no.1 has various mechanical defects. He has also submitted
the affidavit of Shri V. K. Kulkarni, automobile engineer who is surveyor
and loss assessor, who has submitted in his affidavit that there was a
variance in engine number as stated above and the same had
manufacturing defects. Thus, there is sufficient evidence on record to
hold that the tractor in question was resold and had various
manufacturing defects.
15. Appellants contention is that the District Forum has passed
exparte order and he was not given any opportunity to hear therefore the
case be remanded back to the District Forum. In fact the District Forum
in their order in question have mentioned that the notice about the
complaint was sent to the appellant by speed post. The complainant i.e.
respondent no.1 has also submitted that he had sent the said notice
through fax to the appellant. Admittedly, respondent no.2 & 3 are the
dealers of the appellant no.1, therefore when there was complaint in the
Consumer Forum the respondent no.2 & 3 who are the dealers must
have also informed to the company about the same. There are therefore
9 F.A.No.2455-05
grounds to believe that the appellant has avoided to remain present
before the Forum. Even after the Judgment and Order in question was
passed and sanctioned to the appellant no action has been taken against
the dealer i.e. respondent no. 2 & 3. No action of replace of tractor was
also taken by the appellant.
16. It is also the appellant's case that it is the respondent no. 2
& 3 who have sold the tractor to the respondent no.1. Even the allegation
of delivery of old tractor in respect of new tractor is against the
respondent no. 2 & 3. That inspite of these facts on record, the District
Forum has exonerated both these respondents and entire responsibility
is illegally fixed against the appellant only. It is also submitted by the
appellant that in the judgment and order passed by the Forum below the
replies given against the issues raised are in negative in respect of the
appellant however, in the final order it is only against the appellant the
order of replacement of tractor or refund of amount has been passed,
which is injustice against the present appellant. In fact it reveals from
reasoning of the various issues as given by the Forum in their order, the
issue no. 1,2,3 the appellant no.1 i.e. original respondent no.1 has also
been held responsible along with respondent no.2 & 3. Therefore we are
also of the opinion that it is not only the manufacturer of the tractor i.e.
appellant but the dealer the respondent no.2 & 3 are also responsible
and liable. In the judgment given by the Kerala State Commission in
Appeal No. 913 & 915/1999 as decided on 19.09.2000 which is relied
upon by the respondent no.1 for the defect in printer the dealers are also
held liable. The same principle applies in the instant case. The tractor is
sold by the dealer to the respondent no.1 which has found to have
manufacturing defects. Not only that, but it is revealsed that the
respondent no. 2 & 3 have given old tractor instead of new tractor to the
respondent no1. Therefore both the dealers' i.e. respondent no. 2 & 3 are
equally responsible and liable to pay the damages to the respondent
no.1. The contention of the appellant that as per Sec. 13 (b) of C. P. Act
the District Forum before arriving at conclusion the tractor having
manufacturing defect it should have obtained experts opinion. However,
10 F.A.No.2455-05
this contention can not be accepted as the allegation in present case is
that the respondent no.1 has given old tractor in place of new tractor by
its dealer i.e. respondent no. 2 & 3.
17. In view of our above said observations we find that the Forum
below has not considered the liability of the respondent no. 2 & 3 and
erred in directing the appellant only for replacement of tractor or for
refund of the cost of the said tractor. We therefore modify the order to the
extent of holding liable both the respondent no. 2 & 3 as they are the
dealers of the said tractor. Hence, we pass the following order.
*ORDER*
1. Appeal is partly allowed.
2. Appellant along with respondent no. 2 & 3 are individually
 and jointly directed to replace the tractor in question with a
 new tractor of the same company within 30 days from the
 date of receipt of this order or to refund the cost of the
 tractor which is Rs. 4,49,515/- with interest @ 9 % p.a. from
 the date of complaint till its realization.
3. Rest of the order is maintained as it is.
4. Copy of the order be furnished to the parties.
(K. B. Gawali) (Mrs.Uma S. Bora) (S. G. Deshmukh)
 Member Member Presiding Judicial Member
Kalyankar
